case_title: Santosh @ Rajesh @ Gopal v. State of Madhya Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34, s.120B; Arms Act s.25(1-B)(A)
evidence_type: Circumstantial (recovery of pistol, ballistic report, disclosure statement); no eyewitness implicating the accused
confession: None by the accused. A co-accused's disclosure statement (Exhibit P-35) was relied on by the prosecution to show discovery of the pistol under ss.8 and 27, not as a confession of the accused
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of murder and related offences (IPC ss.302, 34, 120B; Arms Act s.25(1-B)(A)); sentence not stated
neutral_facts: On the night of 13 November 2011, at about 9.30 p.m., the victim and his mother were sleeping at their house in a village in Dewas district. Someone called the victim's name from outside and the victim opened the door. The victim's mother testified that she heard a gunshot and ran towards him. A second shot then struck the victim in the chest and he fell. Going outside, the mother saw the victim's wife and son standing on the opposite side of the house. She also saw two individuals with covered faces fleeing on a motorcycle. A country-made pistol was later recovered from the accused. A ballistic report found that the bullet recovered from the victim's body had been fired from that pistol. The prosecution case was that the location of the pistol was disclosed by a co-accused, who has since died, and that this disclosure led to the recovery of the pistol and to the arrest of the accused. No eyewitness identified the accused as a participant in the shooting. The case against the accused rested on the recovery of the pistol and the ballistic report. A First Information Report was registered on 13 November 2011, and a chargesheet was filed against several persons.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a gunshot wound to the chest
premeditation_planning: Not stated. The prosecution alleged hired killers, but the Court made no finding on premeditation or planning
key_evidence_accepted: Recovery of the pistol (Exhibit P-6) from the accused; ballistic report (Exhibit P-57) linking the pistol to the bullet (Exhibit B-1) recovered from the victim's body
witness_credibility: Not stated as a credibility assessment. The Court noted that no eyewitness implicates the accused
bail_history: Granted by the Supreme Court on suspension of sentence on 08.04.2024
trial_duration: offence: 13.11.2011; trial judgment: not given (trial court verdict dated 30.11.2017 is stated, but no trial judgment date is given separately); High Court: 18.10.2022; Supreme Court: 19 September 2024
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): Ms. Shweta Garg, Ashish Gopal Garg, Rakesh Garg, Advocates. State of Madhya Pradesh: Nachiketa Joshi, Senior Advocate / A.A.G., with Pashupathi Nath Razdan, Pushpender Singh, Mirza Kayesh Begg, Ms. Maitreyee Jagat Joshi, Ms. Ruby, Advocates
investigation_status: FIR registered; chargesheet filed; trial completed with verdict
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside
prosecution_argument: The pistol was recovered from the accused, and its discovery was based on the co-accused's disclosure statement. The ballistic report links the pistol to the fatal bullet. Both are admissible under ss.8 and 27 of the Evidence Act
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain excluding every hypothesis of innocence. Discovery under ss.8 and 27 of the Evidence Act is assessed by considering alternative hypotheses. Further evidence linking the accused to the actual murder is required
precedent_relied_upon: Hanumant v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1952) 2 SCC 71; Sharad Birdhichand Sharda v. State of Maharashtra [1985] 1 SCR 88 : (1984) 4 SCC 116; Perumal Raja v. State [2024] 1 SCR 87; Mohmed Inayatullah v. State of Maharashtra [1976] 1 SCR 715 : (1976) 1 SCC 828; State of Maharashtra v. Suresh [1999] Supp. 5 SCR 215 : (2000) 1 SCC 471
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds and sureties cancelled; pending applications disposed of
